title: Aerie
slugLine: REAL Spring: an Instagram plan for March and April to make aerieREAL the loudest human story in fashion this spring.

research.problem: aerie stopped retouching its models in 2014. This spring it takes aerieREAL a step further: no AI-generated models either. The plan has to make “no AI” ==the most human thing in fashion this spring==, and still sell the spring and beachwear collections.

stakeholders.name: aerie
stakeholders.note: aerieREAL: no retouching since 2014, and now no AI

stakeholders.name: Pamela Anderson
stakeholders.note: The headline act of the no-AI campaign

stakeholders.name: aerieREAL models and creators
stakeholders.note: Shoot their own days in aerie: aerie briefs the fit, they keep the caption

stakeholders.name: aerieREALmakers
stakeholders.note: Twelve get spring product early and send back three clips each

stakeholders.name: The anti-AI crowd
stakeholders.note: Drawn to a brand that shows real people

headlines.headline: Likes on a creator’s beach day in aerie beachwear, the season’s most-liked post.
Likes on one unretouched Polaroid of Pamela Anderson, the season’s second most-liked post.
Likes on the spring break giveaway, the third most-liked post.
Likes on a white-on-black “No AI” statement reel: a statement about real people drew far less than real people in frame.

rows.goal: Brand awareness for aerieREAL as the anti-AI brand
rows.target: “Never AI generated” on most posts and in the bio; five Pamela × no-AI posts

rows.kpi: 90K+ likes on the creator beach day

rows.goal: Sell the spring and beachwear collections
rows.target: Eight collection posts, always on an aerieREAL model or in a natural place

rows.goal: Turn lurkers into followers and find new aerieREAL models
rows.target: Four community posts: the spring break giveaway and two REALmaker open calls

insights.evidence: Posts with a face attached, like Pamela Anderson or an aerieREAL creator, drew far more likes, and the creator collaborations had the highest average engagement of the season.

insights.insight: The best collaboration doesn’t read as an ad.
insights.evidence: The top creator posts looked like the creators’ own days; the aerie branding only showed in the caption.
Carousels were the main and most popular format: one post shows several styles, outfits and models to a broad audience.

insights.insight: An analog look backs up the no-AI claim.
insights.evidence: The Unprompted series’ vintage set, with flowers, warm colours and Polaroid cameras, was a consistent hook, and Polaroid runs a similar campaign of its own.

design.lead: Twenty-six posts across March and April, built around three big swings, four content pillars and five recurring series, under one rule: ==a face in frame beats a statement about faces==.

blocks.title: The three big swings

clauses.label: The creator beach day, 90K+ likes
clauses.text: her beach, her caption, aerie’s beachwear. The brief covers the fit, never the frame.

clauses.label: Pamela, on Polaroid, 70K+ likes
clauses.text: one instant photo, unretouched: the cheapest frame of the season and the one that travels furthest.

clauses.label: The spring break giveaway, 15K+ likes
clauses.text: one sweepstakes and one loud week of comments, the fastest way to turn lurkers into followers.

blocks.note: Everything else in the plan exists to set these three up.

blocks.title: Content pillars

items.label: REAL, Not Rendered: Pamela × no AI
REAL Community: giveaway and open calls

blocks.note: Creators and REAL models are shown inside their own days: a walk through New York, a matcha, a hike, the beach. The collection is shown as clothes people live in and then fall asleep in, never as a product shot. No post is behind-the-scenes or type alone: the behind-the-scenes texture runs through the other pillars.

blocks.title: Recurring series

clauses.label: Pamela Anderson × aerieREAL, 8 posts
clauses.text: the headline act: sourdough, flowers, Polaroid cameras, and a straight-faced read of AI ad copy.

clauses.label: aerieREAL collabs, 6 posts
clauses.text: creators and REAL models in their own days, each one bringing their own fanbase.

clauses.label: No AI × aerieREAL, 5 posts
clauses.text: the position stated plainly: one bold statement card, then collages of real people to back it up.

clauses.label: Comfy spring fits, 5 posts
clauses.text: lace shorties, graphic tees and the Alumni set: the whole outfit on a closet wall, then the same outfit on a real body.

clauses.label: Vacay vibes and open calls, 4 posts
clauses.text: the team in Palm Springs, the giveaway, then the REALmaker open calls.

blocks.note: Each series recurs, so the feed reads as chapters, not one-offs. The tag worth trademarking is “Unprompted”: it reads as spontaneity and as a jab at prompt-written advertising at once.

blocks.title: Format mix
blocks.note: Every collection post is a carousel, for several outfits, angles and a story in one post. Reels carry the Pamela shoot, the behind-the-scenes montages and the Unprompted series, and a reel always has a person in it. Single images are rationed: one frame has to earn the whole slot.

blocks.title: Production

clauses.label: Creator shoot days, 2
clauses.text: four aerieREAL collaborators, in their own cities and on the beach. They shoot most of it themselves.

clauses.label: Pamela days, 2
clauses.text: the whole collaboration in one window: the flowers, the sourdough, the field, the AI-copy read. Film cameras on set.

clauses.label: Palm Springs trip, 1
clauses.text: the team trip doubles as the Vacay Vibes shoot.

clauses.label: UGC clips, 36
clauses.text: twelve REALmakers get spring product early and send three clips each. Saturdays and stories run on these.

clauses.label: Statement cards, 2
clauses.text: hand-set type: “we stopped retouching in 2014” and “we don’t use AI”.

blocks.note: Non-negotiable in every brief and every contract: zero generative AI, zero retouching.
